title: Active larvae are adapted to their own conditions as fully as adults

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Active larvae are adapted to their own conditions as fully as adults

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whenever an embryo or larva becomes active and must provide for itself, it is as perfectly adapted to its conditions of life as the adult, and such adaptations can make the larvae of allied species differ as much as or more than their adults, though most larvae still follow the law of embryonic resemblance.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The period of activity may come on earlier or later in life; but whenever it comes on, the adaptation of the larva to its conditions of life is just as perfect and as beautiful as in the adult animal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “EMBRYOLOGY, laws of, explained by variations not supervening at an early age, and being inherited at a corresponding age”. Scope: animals with free-living larval stages (e.g. insects, crustaceans, cirripedes)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.47

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative performance and disparity are testable proxies, but perfection is not operationally defined. Existing public data are narrow and scattered, allowing only restricted tests.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define adaptation as survival or performance relative to feasible alternatives, then compare active larval and adult stage-specific performance and phylogenetic disparity in species with free-living larvae. Equivalent standardized performance and occasional greater larval disparity support the measurable portion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Perfectly adapted' has no absolute measurable scale.

Survivorship creates strong ascertainment bias.

Stage-specific fitness data are scattered and environmentally contingent.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.35

discriminating power: 0.48

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The disparity comparison is a genuine empirical clause and can be attempted for fishes and some arthropods with existing trait tables and matrices. The perfection clause has no decision threshold that preserves the wording, which caps operationalizability and discriminating power. Available data therefore test a proxy in a subset of taxa, and only that proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For free-living larvae, compare trait-environment fit and among-species morphological disparity at the larval stage with the same quantities in adults of the same species. The disparity clause is confirmed if allied larvae differ at least as much as their adults where larval ecology differs, and refuted if larvae remain more uniform than adults despite active, divergent habits; 'as perfect' has no separate numerical threshold.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Larval ecology is tabulated for many fishes and for a few insect and crustacean groups, not for free-living larvae in general.

'As perfect and as beautiful' does not name a measurement that a dataset could fail.

Larval and adult disparity are comparable only when both stages are scored on the same characters, which is uncommon.

data existence: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.4
